name: Light Rosolane Purple
lede: Light Rosolane Purple is a lighter step off [[berry-pink|Rosolane Purple]], a strong purplish red Ridgway plated in 1912 from an unexplained name.

sections.title: A modifier on an unexplained name
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[berry-pink|Rosolane Purple]], itself the deeper partner to Rosolane Pink in Ridgway's 1912 atlas, where "rosolane" is left unglossed [1]. Ridgway's plate XXVI, hue 69', tone b, is the source, and the ISCC-NBS system separately filed the step in 1955 as block 248 [1]. Measured, it is lighter than its parent at a close chroma (lightness 63 against 50), keeping the same hot, purplish-pink cast [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[china-pink|China Pink]], 2.7 units away, almost the same, with [[pink-orchid|Pink Orchid]] close behind at 3.2, duller [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. A purplish pink this saturated sits outside the range of pigments most painters working from natural dyes had on hand [2].

origin.named_after: a descriptive modifier: light + Rosolane Purple; "rosolane" itself is undocumented
origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature
